## Findings by Section

**CUSTOMER DEFINITION** — PARTIAL
"Support engineers" is a role, and the Background section gives it a real
situational hook ("Engineers spend significant time reading through threads
before they can respond or take action") — that's closer to a moment than a
bare role name, and this persona's own bias disclosure applies here: Flowdesk
is presumably an internal tool with a well-understood user, so a full
PR/FAQ-style customer narrative may be more than this feature needs. `◎
AMBIENT?` — if "support engineer" is an already-understood role at your org,
add it to SPARRING_CONTEXT.md Section 5 (customer context) so this stops
getting flagged.
What's still genuinely missing: **who is NOT the customer.** Is this for L1
support only, or also engineers who get escalated tickets, or non-support
roles who view tickets? Unstated — a real gap regardless of how well-known
"support engineer" is. (WARN, not BLOCK.)

**PROBLEM STATEMENT** — PASS
Background states the problem (context-switching, time lost reading thread
history) before "What We Are Building" describes the solution. Correct
Working-Backwards order.

**SUCCESS METRICS** — FAIL
Evidence: Background states the actual goal is to "reduce time-to-first-action."
None of the four ACs measure that. AC2 (90% accuracy against a human-reviewed
test set) measures summary quality, not whether the feature achieves the
outcome it was justified by. As written, this spec could hit 100% on every
AC and still not know whether time-to-first-action improved at all.
Recommendation: what is the target reduction in time-to-first-action, and
how/when is it measured (e.g., median time from ticket-open to first reply,
compared pre/post launch)? A quality gate (AC2) is not a substitute for an
outcome metric.
Confidence: high — this isn't a matter of taste, the spec names its own goal
and then doesn't measure it.

**FAILURE CONDITIONS** — FAIL
Evidence: not present anywhere in the spec.
No signal is defined for "this isn't working." Candidates that come to mind
but aren't stated: a thumbs-down rate above some threshold, accuracy
regression detected post-launch, or time-to-first-action *not* moving.
Given engineers may act on a summary's contents when handling a live
customer ticket, "we shipped it and nobody's monitoring for it being wrong"
is a materially different risk than a UI feature no one uses — this pushes
the decision closer to Type 1 (harder to walk back cleanly) than the spec's
current thin framing treats it.
Recommendation: what tells us this failed, and by when after launch?

**SCOPE DEFINITION** — PARTIAL
All three out-of-scope items are stated but none carry a reason. `◎
AMBIENT?` — if these exclusions are obvious internally (e.g., "no OCR
pipeline exists yet" for attachments, "translation isn't in this quarter's
roadmap" for multi-language), add them to SPARRING_CONTEXT.md Section 4 so
this stops flagging. Until then this is a WARN, not a BLOCK: an unstated
reason invites the exclusion to get silently relitigated mid-build.

## Assumptions Log
1. Engineers will trust and act on AI-generated summaries without any way to
   correct them (editing is explicitly out of scope) — Validated: unknown.
2. "Accuracy" against a human-reviewed test set is assumed to be a clean,
   measurable concept for a generative summary — Validated: unknown. (Summary
   quality is rarely binary correct/incorrect; this may need a defined
   rubric before AC2 is testable at all — flagging for QA Functional to
   pick up, not resolving here.)
3. Thumbs up/down feedback (AC3) is assumed to feed back into something
   (model tuning, alerting, a review queue) — the spec captures the signal
   but never says what happens to it. Validated: unknown.
